pr_comments:
> I initially was trying to use a `BuiltinFn`, but it turned out that it doesn't even get to `accessHelper` [...]
> This might be avoidable with the global type definition [...]

Yes, I believe so.

##
> or by introducing a new way that allows mapping identifiers to `ts.Node`'s. This might be useful for your PR that fixes inlined ts helper functions too.

Indeed. Looking forward to see what you'll come up with.

##
> I think we don't want to add support for `Object.assign` in the `Interpreter`, but rather only handle it in ngcc (with the reason of supporting transpiled libraries).

TBH, I don't see why :grin:
`Object.assign()` is not much different than other `BuiltinFn`s (such as `Array.prototype.slice()`) and if there are `Object.assign()` instances that are _not_ a result of transpilation, it would be weird to support them in ngcc, but not ngtsc.

##
> If we'd add it to the interpreter, then I could imagine us arguing adding more functions like `Object.keys` etc. 

Which is bad, because... 😕 :grin:

Fair enough. Maybe @petebacondarwin remembers why the change has been made. IIRC we already chatted about this on Slack, and it seemed like it was because of the mocked file system which did not contain the TypeScript default library files.

a) it would be faster to process if we loaded in as few files into the program as possible
b) the mock file systems did not include these files

If everything works as expected with this removed, and there is no significant performance penalty, then I am happy.

review_comments: OOC, have you checked whether removing `noLib` affects performance noticeably?
I didn't. It has been enabled in the past too, but just seems to have been disabled when the mocked file system has been introduced. Can surely do some measurements if needed.

Fair enough. If it has been there before, it can't be too bad :grin:

@petebacondarwin, any idea why was this removed in https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/16d7dde2ad89eb4610c74da63e0e4b00afb8b577#diff-ac19368dcc489893e10fcaa6ff9436aeR48 (just to make sure there is nothing we should take into account)?

Probably because it was a fair bit of work to introduce the default library typings into the abstract filesystem.

I doubt including an extra .d.ts file or two will cause any performance issues.
Would it make sense to have this in the `TypescriptHost` instead (in case someone uses `Object.assign()` directly)?
I think the idea is to keep ngtsc as lightweight as possible?

The idea was that we just want to support `__assign` and `Object.assign` in ngcc for backwards compatibility. Previously the spread operator worked fine because the actual spread AST got put into the `metadata.json`. So, explicitly using `Object.assign` didn't work in ngc either.

I don't feel strongly about it. I just don't feel like there is a compelling reason to put it into ngtsc. Happy to change it if you all feel strongly about it.
Makes sense. Let's keep it in ngcc only for now.
